Joanna — thanks for the context and the materials. Quick summary from our side: Redwood typically anchors this role at L5 senior IC by default for platform engineering ICs. Manager placement is allowed, but we treat it as a track decision (manager vs IC) based on sustained people management scope, direct reports count (>2) and long-term role expectations.

Operationally, when a hiring manager requests a manager placement that would exceed the posted band we do one of the following:
- Approve a manager variance (one-time base uplift or slight anchor shift) with finance/people Ops signoff and a conditional performance/role review at 6 months; or
- Keep candidate at Senior IC with an explicit scope-of-work addendum if the manager duties are limited/temporary.

For Acme's ask: if the hiring manager believes Aria will have 3+ direct reports within 3 months and be accountable for people workflows end-to-end, we can consider an L5 Manager placement with a manager variance. To proceed we'll need:
1) A short Mutual Action Plan listing the expected team size and milestones (I attached a template MAP).
2) Finance confirmation of budget and any HC transfer note.
3) Written confirmation from the hiring manager on direct-report timeline and org chart (1-page).

If you can share the MAP filled and confirmation from hiring manager by EOD tomorrow we can route for an expedited variance approval.

Attachments: MAP_Acme_AriaGomez.xlsx

> For Acme's ask: if the hiring manager believes Aria will have 3+ direct reports within 3 months and be accountable for people workflows end-to-end, we can consider an L5 Manager placement with a manager variance.
> 
> To proceed we'll need: 1) MAP, 2) Finance confirmation, 3) Hiring manager confirmation.

Adding color from compensation/people Ops: an L5 Manager at market would likely be ~6–9% above the band midpoint for the IC anchor in this discipline if we push title without adding HC. We have two practical levers:
- Approve a one-time manager variance (recommended when manager responsibilities are real and immediate). This preserves future comp equity by flagging the hire and scheduling a 6-month review.
- Approve the candidate at Senior IC (L5) but include a documented manager shadowing path + promotion trigger at 6 months.

Given Acme's stated timeline and that the hiring manager expects hires to own direct reports quickly, I'm inclined to recommend the manager variance with these conditions:
- Manager variance = +8% base uplift to the offer anchor;
- Manager performance review at 6 months with clear promotion/comp re-eval criteria;
- Headcount remains within Q3 HC planning (finance to confirm).

Laura — can you sign off on the variance as described so we can get this back to Joanna? If finance needs different phrasing/controls, happy to iterate.

Thanks,

Thanks everyone — reviewed the MAP and the hiring manager note (attached). Approving the L5 Manager placement with the following conditions:

- Manager variance: one-time base uplift of 8% to the L5 anchor for this hire.
- Manager bonus target: set at 7% of base for first 12 months (pro-rated).
- Conditional clause: 6-month performance and scope review with explicit promotion/comp re-eval criteria; if manager responsibilities are not met to the described level, comp reversion terms apply.
- HC: Finance confirms this will be charged to Q3 discretionary headcount (see HR-1123).

Please prepare the offer with manager variance language and the conditional 6-month review clause. Joanna — once you send the updated MAP and the signed hiring manager attestation, we will issue the formal variance term sheet and proceed with the offer.
